overview: White builds the e4-d4 centre with Nc3, and Black keeps the Modern by ...d6, ...c6 or ...c5, delaying ...Nf6. White follows with Be3, Qd2, f4 or Nf3 and Bc4, hoping for a kingside attack against Black's cramped game. Black counters with ...c6, ...Nd7 and ...e5, or ...c5, using the g7 bishop. The positions are less forcing than the Pirc but White usually has more space.

white_ideas.idea: Be3, Qd2, f3 and O-O-O or h4 for a kingside attack
Nf3, Be2 and O-O, a solid space edge

black_ideas.idea: ...d6, ...c6, ...Nd7 and ...e5 or ...b5 to counter in the centre
...c5 or ...Nc6 with the g7 bishop pressing d4

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 centre against d6/g6, Black breaks with ...e5 or ...c5

character.notes: Hypermodern and flexible, Black may be cramped but is hard to break; no forced lines.

approach.notes: The g6/Bg7/d6 set-up can be used against almost anything, so system.

sublines_that_differ.name: Modern: 3.Nc3 c6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c6

character.reason: Space for White, resilient set-up for Black, not forcing.

approach.reason: Modern set-up playable against nearly everything.

level.reason: Few forced lines, plans need judgement.

plans.reason: Black lets White take the centre and attacks it from the flank.
